purpose: This medication is used to treat tension headaches that are moderate to severe and have not responded to other treatments. It combines four ingredients that each play a different role in relieving headache pain. Your doctor may prescribe it when simpler pain relievers are not enough to help you feel better.
how_it_works: Butalbital is a mild sedative that relaxes muscle tension, which is often a big part of tension headaches. Aspirin is a pain reliever and anti-inflammatory that helps reduce the pain signal. Codeine is a mild opioid that works in your brain to block pain, and caffeine helps the other ingredients work better and faster by improving blood flow and boosting their effectiveness.
common_side_effects: You may feel drowsy, dizzy, or lightheaded. Some people feel nauseous, have an upset stomach, or feel short of breath. You might also feel a little sedated or have trouble concentrating. These effects are usually mild but let your doctor know if they bother you.
warnings: This medication contains codeine, which is an opioid, so there is a risk of dependence or addiction if used too often or for too long. Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine — it can be very dangerous. Do not drive or operate heavy machinery until you know how this medicine affects you. Do not take more than prescribed, and never share it with others. People with stomach ulcers, bleeding problems, kidney disease, liver problems, or a history of substance abuse should use this medication with extra caution. Taking it too frequently can actually cause rebound headaches, making your headaches worse over time.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is one or two capsules every four hours as needed for pain. You should not take more than six capsules in a single day. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribed, and do not use it more often than directed to avoid dependence or rebound headaches.
